title: Clo-HDnn: Continual On-Device Learning Accelerator with Hyperdimensional Computing via Progressive Search
problem: On-device continual learning requires efficient gradient-free training for edge devices with strict power and memory constraints.
motivation: Emerging edge AI applications demand continual learning without cloud connectivity; hyperdimensional computing offers a gradient-free alternative enabling efficient incremental model updates.
method: The system uses hyperdimensional computing (machine learning based on comparing high-dimensional vectors) to enable fast, gradient-free training on edge devices—avoiding the heavy backpropagation computation that drains power and memory. It combines two efficiency techniques: Kronecker encoding (a structured way to build vectors) and weight clustering feature extraction (grouping similar weights to reduce learning complexity). The core innovation is progressive search, which cuts query complexity by 61% by encoding and comparing only partial query vectors instead of full ones, letting the device learn continuously from new data within its power budget.
key_novelty: Progressive search reduces hyperdimensional computing query complexity by 61% through partial hypervector encoding, enabling efficient on-device continual learning.
contributions: Specialized accelerator for hyperdimensional computing and on-device continual learning
Gradient-free learning enabling efficient knowledge updates
Progressive search reducing encoder complexity by 61%
4.66 TFLOPS/W (feature extraction) and 3.78 TOPS/W (classifier) energy efficiency
limitations: Progressive search applicability limited to datasets where partial queries maintain classification confidence.
primary_theme: hyperdimensional computing for on-device continual learning
